title: NHS: Missed or late periods
keywords: late period missed periods menstrual cycle irregular causes stress weight exercise contraception pregnancy
content: A late or missed period can happen for many reasons, including pregnancy, stress, sudden weight loss, being overweight, too much exercise, or some forms of contraception. If pregnancy is possible, a pregnancy test can help clarify the cause. Contact a healthcare professional if you are concerned, miss periods repeatedly, or have other symptoms.

title: NHS: Doing a pregnancy test
keywords: pregnancy test pregnant late missed period when test
content: Most pregnancy tests are most reliable from the first day of a missed period. If you do not know when your next period is due, test at least 21 days after unprotected sex. Follow the instructions that come with the test.

title: NHS: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
keywords: pcos polycystic ovary syndrome irregular periods acne hair fertility diagnosis
content: PCOS is one possible cause of irregular periods, but irregular periods can have many causes. A healthcare professional assesses symptoms and may arrange tests; a late period alone cannot establish that someone has PCOS.

title: NHS: Period problems
keywords: period pain heavy bleeding period problems doctor healthcare professional severe bleeding urgent
content: Period problems can have different causes. Seek medical advice if period pain or bleeding is severe, affects daily life, or is a change from what is usual for you. Sudden severe pain or very heavy bleeding may need urgent assessment.

title: NHS: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)
keywords: pms premenstrual syndrome symptoms before period mood changes irritability bloating breast tenderness headaches tiredness
content: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) can cause symptoms in the days or weeks before a period. Symptoms can include mood changes, irritability, feeling upset or anxious, tiredness, difficulty sleeping, bloating, breast tenderness, headaches and changes in appetite. Symptoms can vary between people and may change over time.

title: NHS: Period pain
keywords: period pain cramps menstrual pain abdominal pain painful periods dysmenorrhoea
content: Period pain is common and usually happens around the start of a period. It can feel like painful cramps in the lower abdomen and may last for several days. See a healthcare professional if the pain is severe, getting worse, or affecting daily activities.

title: NHS: Mental health and wellbeing
keywords: mental health stress anxiety depression mood wellbeing sleep emotional health
content: Mental health can affect how a person thinks, feels and behaves. Looking after mental wellbeing can include getting enough sleep, staying physically active, maintaining connections with other people and seeking support when difficulties are affecting everyday life.

title: NHS: Women's health
keywords: womens health periods reproductive health contraception pregnancy menstrual health health
content: Women's health includes areas such as menstrual health, reproductive health, pregnancy and contraception. Symptoms that are persistent, severe, unusual for you or affecting daily life may need assessment from a healthcare professional.
